inputs.text: Appeals to culture and public consent can turn majority discomfort into a veto over equal rights. Traditions change; they should not be used to excuse discrimination. Calling equality a “fashionable global debate” or an “outside” pressure shifts attention from people facing exclusion to anxiety about social change. As described, Mahama’s framing risks putting social order ahead of vulnerable people. Cultural life deserves respect, but equal treatment under the law should not depend on whether it is popular.
